# `aitbc crosschain bridge`

Bridge tokens to a target chain via a real signed bridge lock. The wallet signs the lock request (same payload as ``/rpc/bridge/lock``); the node creates a real BRIDGE_LOCK transaction. ``bridge_id`` equals the transfer ID and the source-chain transaction hash.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc crosschain bridge [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--source-chain` | text | — | yes | Source chain ID |
| `--target-chain` | text | — | yes | Target chain ID |
| `--token` | text | — | yes | Token to bridge |
| `--amount` | decimal | — | yes | Amount to bridge (AIT) |
| `--recipient` | text | — | no | Recipient address on the target chain (defaults to the sender) |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet name or file path for signing |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL (source-chain producer) |
| `--wait` | flag | `false` | no | Poll status until the transfer reaches a terminal state |
| `--timeout` | integer | `300` | no | Seconds to wait with --wait (default 300) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc crosschain bridge --source-chain <source_chain> --target-chain <target_chain> --token <token> --amount <amount>
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc crosschain bridge --source-chain <source_chain> --target-chain <target_chain> --token <token> --amount <amount> --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
